candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Epistola ad Marcellinum §30
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Marcellinum de Interpretatione Psalmorum (Letter to Marcellinus on the Interpretation of the Psalms), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 27 (1857). The Letter is Athanasius's principal pastoral-spiritual work — a personal letter to Marcellinus (recovering from illness) explaining how to use each Psalm as prayer for specific spiritual circumstances. Hermeneutic anchor for the Tewahedo Office (Säʿatat) Psalter-recitation tradition.
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Marcellinum §30 (c. 350 AD)

'Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee' (LXX 118:11 — en tē kardia mou ekrypsa ta logia sou hopōs an mē hamartō soi) — Athanasius marks Ps 119 (LXX 118) — the longest-Psalm, structured by the Hebrew-alphabet — as the WORD-INTERNALIZATION PARADIGM in the Letter to Marcellinus. The praying-soul does not merely-recite-the-word but HIDES-IT-IN-THE-HEART (ekrypsa en tē kardia) as protective-talisman-against-sin. The logia (oracles/divine-utterances) are Spirit-breathed-Scripture, and their-hiding-in-the-heart is the Spirit's-work-of-sanctifying-memory. Athanasius's pastoral-instruction: memorize the Psalter completely; the soul that knows-the-Psalter-by-heart has the Spirit's-prayer-vocabulary always-at-hand.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Marcellinum §30. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.
